m1.title: Fix 1 (THE BLOCKER): give each of the 5 named negative tests an in-method positive control, then run the mechanical disable-attack
m1.imperative: Vertical slice 1. In tests/test_code_map.py, rewrite these 5 methods so each contains, in the SAME method, an assertion that a known-should-flag mutation (the existing WIDTH -> WIDTH*2 real body change on widget-spin) DOES flag, using the same fixture/build path/assertion mechanism already in the method -- not a separate new test: test_stale_tag_first_extraction_flags_nothing (append a second extraction after a real change, assert it flags), test_stale_tag_does_not_flag_a_reformat_across_two_extractions (append a third extraction with a real change on top, assert it flags), test_stale_tag_does_not_flag_an_unrelated_anchor (assert widget-spin IS in the stale set alongside asserting holder-hold is not), test_stale_tag_render_report_does_not_flag_a_reformat (append a control build with a real change, assert stale_tags == ['widget-spin']), test_stale_tag_render_report_does_not_fail_the_build (after the exit-0 assertion, read render_report.json fresh and assert stale_tags == ['widget-spin'], since exit-0 alone cannot distinguish advisory from disabled). Do this for ALL 5 -- a partial rewrite leaves survivors. Then write and run .agent-work/issue-456/evidence/g6_disable_attack.py: it forces `stale = []` immediately after the real computation in extract.py's run() (locating the anchor programmatically, not via a fragile hardcoded string), reruns the `stale_tag` selector, asserts all 5 named tests are in the FAILED set, restores extract.py in a finally block (even on assertion failure), confirms `git status --porcelain -- scripts/code_map/extract.py` is clean, and reruns the selector to confirm green again -- exiting 0 only if every check holds, printing a summary dict either way. Attest c1 (rewrite done, diff reviewed). c2 is the normal-mode selector green. c3 is the disable-attack script itself, run for real -- not reasoned about.

postconditions.statement: all 5 named negative tests rewritten with an in-method positive control using the same fixture/build path/assertion mechanism; diff reviewed
closing selector green in normal (unmutated) mode
mechanical disable-attack script exits 0: all 5 named tests failed under the forced stale=[] mutation, extract.py reverted clean, selector green again afterward

constraints: do not satisfy the requirement with a separate new positive test elsewhere -- the control lives in the SAME method

allowed scope: scripts/code_map/extract.py, scripts/code_map/render.py, tests/test_code_map.py only

Assert the new test now passes (code 0, previous store treated as absent, one actionable stdout line). Check c2.
